esql_query:
TS metrics-googlecloudmonitoringreceiver.otel-default
| WHERE TRANGE(?_tstart, ?_tend) AND resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "gce_instance"
| STATS instance_name = MAX(LAST_OVER_TIME(instance_name)),
        avg_cpu_utilization = AVG(AVG_OVER_TIME(compute.googleapis.`com/instance/cpu/utilization`)),
        last_reserved_cores = MAX(LAST_OVER_TIME(compute.googleapis.`com/instance/cpu/reserved_cores`)),
        avg_scheduler_wait = AVG(AVG_OVER_TIME(compute.googleapis.`com/instance/cpu/scheduler_wait_time`)),
        total_ram_used = SUM(AVG_OVER_TIME(compute.googleapis.`com/instance/memory/balloon/ram_used`)),
        total_ram_size = SUM(AVG_OVER_TIME(compute.googleapis.`com/instance/memory/balloon/ram_size`)),
        total_swap_in = SUM(AVG_OVER_TIME(compute.googleapis.`com/instance/memory/balloon/swap_in_bytes_count`)),
        total_swap_out = SUM(AVG_OVER_TIME(compute.googleapis.`com/instance/memory/balloon/swap_out_bytes_count`)),
        max_io_latency = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(compute.googleapis.`com/instance/disk/average_io_latency`)),
        max_io_queue_depth = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(compute.googleapis.`com/instance/disk/average_io_queue_depth`)),
        total_interruptions = SUM(SUM_OVER_TIME(compute.googleapis.`com/instance/interruption_count`))
        BY zone = resource.attributes.zone, project_id = resource.attributes.project_id, instance_id = resource.attributes.instance_id
| EVAL cpu_utilization_pct = avg_cpu_utilization * 100.0, memory_used_pct = total_ram_used * 100.0 / total_ram_size
| LIMIT 1

Consumption riding on or above the ceiling means the VM is burning burst credits and will be throttled to the ceiling once they are exhausted, which shows up as sudden latency.

attributes.description: Seconds per second that this VM's vCPUs were ready to run but not scheduled by the GCE host, equivalent to steal time. Near zero is healthy. Non-zero steal while CPU utilization is low means the physical host is oversubscribed — an infrastructure problem that resizing the VM will not fix. Compare against the same chart on other VMs in the zone.

attributes.description: Balloon-driver memory utilization for this instance, computed as the window-average ram_used divided by the last reported ram_size, both summed across all reporting series for the instance. The denominator is a sum rather than the single max value shown in the RAM Size KPI, because this instance reports roughly 11 concurrent balloon series and the numerator spans all of them - dividing by a single series max would overstate the percentage. This is the hypervisor view of guest memory; filesystem usage and per-process memory are not visible in this pipeline. Approaching 100% signals pressure, but confirm with the swap chart before resizing: a high percentage with zero swap is usually just page cache.

query.esql:
TS metrics-googlecloudmonitoringreceiver.otel-default
| WHERE TRANGE(?_tstart, ?_tend) AND resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "gce_instance"
| STATS ram_used = SUM(AVG_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/memory/balloon/ram_used`)), ram_size = SUM(LAST_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/memory/balloon/ram_size`))
| EVAL `Avg Memory Used %` = 100.0 * ram_used / ram_size, Min = 0, Max = 100
| KEEP `Avg Memory Used %`, Min, Max

attributes.description: Inbound and outbound network throughput for this instance, derived from 60-second delta counters. Ingress inside a VPC is effectively uncapped; egress is limited to roughly 2 Gbps per vCPU, so on a small machine type the sent line hits a ceiling long before the received line does. Sent flattening while received keeps climbing is the signature of that ceiling.

attributes.description: Disk read and write operations per second for this instance. IOPS on size-based Persistent Disk types scale with capacity rather than being independently provisioned, so judge saturation by whether latency and queue depth rise alongside IOPS rather than against any absolute number.

attributes.description: Traffic destined for this instance that VPC firewall rules dropped, packets on the left axis and bytes on the right. These packets never reach the VM, so they are not application errors. A low steady baseline is normal internet background noise. A step change usually follows a firewall policy edit; a sustained spike with no matching CPU or network rise suggests scanning.

attributes.description: Average I/O latency per attached disk device, in microseconds at source. Each device and storage type has its own healthy baseline, so compare a series against its own history rather than across devices. A latency spike accompanied by queue depth growth means the disk is saturated; a spike with a flat queue points to infrastructure degradation, which the disk health table will confirm.

| STATS `I/O Latency` = AVG(AVG_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/disk/average_io_latency`)) BY bucket = TBUCKET(50, ?_tstart, ?_tend), `Device` = attributes.device_name

attributes.description: Every disk device attached to this instance, sorted by performance status and then by worst peak I/O latency, with peak queue depth and provisioned capacity alongside. Because the disk series carry no instance_name, the instance_id column is shown so rows can be tied back to the header identity strip. High latency with a high queue means the device is saturated and needs more capacity; high latency with a near-zero queue points to infrastructure degradation instead.

query.esql:
TS metrics-googlecloudmonitoringreceiver.otel-default
| WHERE TRANGE(?_tstart, ?_tend) AND resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "gce_instance"
| STATS prov_size = MAX(LAST_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/disk/provisioning/size`)), lat_us = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/disk/average_io_latency`)), qdepth = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/disk/average_io_queue_depth`)), perf_active = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/disk/performance_status`)) BY attributes.device_name, attributes.storage_type, attributes.performance_status, resource.attributes.instance_id
| EVAL status_raw = CASE(perf_active == 1, attributes.performance_status, null)
| STATS prov_size = MAX(prov_size), lat_us = MAX(lat_us), qdepth = MAX(qdepth), status_mv = VALUES(status_raw), storage_mv = VALUES(attributes.storage_type) BY device = attributes.device_name, instance_id = resource.attributes.instance_id
| EVAL Status = MV_FIRST(status_mv), Storage = MV_FIRST(storage_mv)
| WHERE lat_us IS NOT NULL
| KEEP device, Status, Storage, lat_us, qdepth, prov_size, instance_id
| SORT Status ASC, lat_us DESC
| LIMIT 10

TS metrics-googlecloudmonitoringreceiver.otel-default
| WHERE TRANGE(?_tstart, ?_tend) AND resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "gce_instance"
| STATS prov_size = MAX(LAST_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/disk/provisioning/size`)), lat_us = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/disk/average_io_latency`)), qdepth = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/disk/average_io_queue_depth`)), perf_active = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/disk/performance_status`)) BY attributes.device_name, attributes.storage_type, attributes.performance_status, resource.attributes.instance_id
| EVAL status_raw = CASE(perf_active == 1, attributes.performance_status, null)
| STATS prov_size = MAX(prov_size), lat_us = MAX(lat_us), qdepth = MAX(qdepth), status_mv = VALUES(status_raw), storage_mv = VALUES(attributes.storage_type) BY device = attributes.device_name, instance_id = resource.attributes.instance_id
| EVAL Status = MV_FIRST(status_mv), Storage = MV_FIRST(storage_mv)
| WHERE lat_us IS NOT NULL
| KEEP device, Status, Storage, lat_us, qdepth, prov_size, instance_id
| SORT Status ASC, lat_us DESC
| LIMIT 10

attributes.description: Seconds of runtime this instance reported per 60-second collection interval. This is not cumulative uptime. A flat line at roughly 60 seconds means the VM ran for the whole interval and is the healthy state. Dips below 60 mean it started or stopped mid-interval; gaps in the line mean it reported nothing at all, which is the closest thing to a downtime signal this pipeline provides.

query.esql:

| STATS `Uptime per interval` = AVG(AVG_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/uptime_total`)) BY bucket = TBUCKET(50, ?_tstart, ?_tend)

attributes.description: Interruption events recorded for this instance in the window, split by type and reason, excluding the 'none' placeholder series. MaintenanceEvent means GCE live-migrated the VM for host maintenance — background noise, and a single event is harmless. Preemption means a Spot VM was reclaimed. This table is empty for a VM that was never interrupted, which is the expected healthy state.

query.esql:
TS metrics-googlecloudmonitoringreceiver.otel-default
| WHERE TRANGE(?_tstart, ?_tend) AND resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "gce_instance" AND attributes.interruption_type != "none"
| STATS events = SUM(SUM_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/interruption_count`)) BY attributes.interruption_type, attributes.interruption_reason, attributes.instance_name
| SORT events DESC
| LIMIT 10

TS metrics-googlecloudmonitoringreceiver.otel-default
| WHERE TRANGE(?_tstart, ?_tend) AND resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "gce_instance" AND attributes.interruption_type != "none"
| STATS events = SUM(SUM_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/interruption_count`)) BY attributes.interruption_type, attributes.interruption_reason, attributes.instance_name
| SORT events DESC
| LIMIT 10
